items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I took a trip to Chicago to see my uncle Nat

ctx.x: We once talked about being stranded. If you did lose all your money and all that. There was a German man you would wire for money?

No, I know what you're referring to. This was in Texas. That was in East Bernard. I can't recall his name right now. But not being stranded. He was a friend of mine. He told me whenever you need something, just wire it. But now the time that I actually was stranded was when I was with this Chauncey Holland or Al Travis I think. It was in a little town in Carbondale, Illinois. And there was an old lady there, another lady. She liked me and she liked the band. So we were living with her and we didn't have another…
And you did make out when you got the money somehow?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Uncle Natty and I were, he was one of my favorite uncles. He was the younger one.

ctx.x: What about Natty? Did you know Natty Dominique when he was down here?

Oh, sure. Uncle Natty and I were, he was one of my favorite uncles. He was the younger one. Uncle Natty. And Uncle Natty went to war. And he was a mutilary in the war. And I remember the first time he came back. And he came to the estate up there on Grey Court Street. He didn't stay too long. And he left in Chicago. And I visited him quite a number of times. After I got my band. And I'd go and play up in the eastern part of the states. And Uncle Natty would be one of the first ones that I would go to see him.…
Did you, in playing, back in the chorus band, in playing stock arrangements and everything, did they change them around much? Not very much. You wouldn't put your own?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: I imagine you know of my uncle in Chicago. He still uses his name Dominique. His name is Natty Dominique

ctx.x: What's your name? Well, sure, Paul. I'll be happy to. My name is Don Albert, professionally, and my family name is Dominique. I imagine you know of my uncle in Chicago. He still uses his name Dominique. His name is Natty Dominique, one of the first trumpet players to leave from New Orleans along with King Oliver and the other guys. And after this, where you are now, we're in San Antonio, Texas. This is my residence, and it's 715 St. James. Been living here for the last five years in this home. We bought this…
This is June the 6th, 1961, and I'm Paul Crawford. You were talking about this fellow, one of the first guys you took, you know, when you left New Orleans? No. A banjo player or something?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: Well, you know, sometimes my uncle, he doesn't like to talk to me.

ctx.x: Well, you know, sometimes my uncle, he doesn't like to talk to me. That's another one of these things that I'm referring to. He doesn't discuss his background. Yeah. If you've ever talked to him, you'll find that he has a good. Yeah, well,
I never had a maiden. Somehow, just almost happened.
